name: Epistemics of regulation

subjectOf.text: Regulation is never grounded in the full set of facts about a technology; it is always premised on a prior selection of the facts that regulators themselves treat as relevant when deciding what, when, and how to intervene.
subjectOf.abstract: In this respect, regulation is always premised on a selection of relevant facts about a particular technology.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531

subjectOf.text: The post truth diagnosis is self defeating as a basis for regulation: if there is no objective basis on which to act, the conclusion is inertia or reproduction of the status quo, which is precisely the regulatory paralysis the diagnosis purports to describe.
subjectOf.abstract: If we live in a post–truth world then we don't have any objective basis on which to act, leading to inertia or the reproduction of the status quo.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531
scope_conditions: if the skeptical post fact account of regulation is accepted
